# Go

Les conventions du projet priment (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/`, `mise.toml`, `Makefile`,
`.golangci.yml`, code voisin). Ce qui suit comble ce qu'ils ne disent pas.

## Outillage

Repère d'abord les tâches du projet (`mise tasks`, `Makefile`, CI) : elles fixent les
versions et les options de lint. À défaut :

```bash
go build ./...
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./chemin/...        # si installé ; reprendre le .golangci.yml du projet
go test ./chemin/du/paquet/ -run 'TestNom' -count=1
go test -race ./chemin/...            # exige cgo et un compilateur C ; si absent, le dire
go mod tidy && git diff --stat go.mod go.sum   # après tout changement de dépendance
```

Version de Go : celle de `go.mod` (directive `go`/`toolchain`), pas celle que tu connais.
Une fonctionnalité récente du langage ou de la bibliothèque standard n'est utilisable que
si cette version la fournit.

## Tests

- Table-driven par défaut, un sous-test par cas nommé :
  ```go
  tests := []struct{ name string; in X; want Y; wantErr bool }{ … }
  for _, tt := range tests {
      t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) { … })
  }
  ```
- `t.Helper()` dans les fonctions utilitaires, `t.Cleanup` plutôt que `defer` dans les
  sous-tests, `t.TempDir()` et `t.Setenv()` pour isoler fichiers et environnement.
- `t.Parallel()` seulement si le test n'a aucun état partagé (variable globale, répertoire,
  port, `~/.config`).
- Compare avec la bibliothèque déjà utilisée par le projet (`testing` seul, `testify`,
  `go-cmp`) ; n'en ajoute pas une.
- Teste le comportement exposé (paquet `x_test` quand c'est possible), pas les détails
  internes. Pas de `time.Sleep` : injecte une horloge ou attends un signal.
- Une erreur attendue se vérifie avec `errors.Is` / `errors.As`, pas par comparaison de
  message.
- Fuzzing (`func FuzzX(f *testing.F)`) pour les parseurs et décodeurs d'entrées externes.
- Aucun test ne doit toucher au répertoire personnel, au trousseau, à Docker ni à un port
  fixe de l'hôte sans isolation.

## Écrire

- **Erreurs** : jamais ignorées (`_ =` justifié en commentaire). Enrobe avec contexte :
  `fmt.Errorf("lire %s: %w", path, err)`. Pas de `panic` hors initialisation.
  Pas de message commençant par une majuscule ni finissant par un point.
- **Interfaces** : petites, définies côté consommateur ; on accepte des interfaces, on
  retourne des types concrets.
- **`context.Context`** : premier paramètre, jamais stocké dans une structure, propagé aux
  appels bloquants ; `defer cancel()` juste après `WithCancel`/`WithTimeout`.
- **Goroutines** : chacune a un propriétaire et une condition d'arrêt (contexte, canal
  fermé, `errgroup`). Pas de goroutine lancée sans moyen de l'attendre. L'émetteur ferme
  le canal, jamais le récepteur.
- **Concurrence** : une map n'est pas sûre en écriture concurrente ; `sync.Mutex` plutôt
  qu'un canal pour protéger un état simple.
- **Boucles** : depuis Go 1.22, la variable de boucle est propre à chaque itération ; ne
  corrige pas ce qui n'est plus un défaut, mais respecte la version de `go.mod`.
- **`defer`** dans une boucle s'exécute à la sortie de la fonction : extraire le corps dans
  une fonction.
- **Slices et maps** : pré-allouer quand la taille est connue ; attention à l'aliasing
  après `append` ; une map `nil` se lit mais ne s'écrit pas.
- **Valeur zéro utile**, constructeurs `NewX` seulement si l'initialisation est
  non triviale. Options fonctionnelles seulement au-delà de 3 ou 4 paramètres optionnels.
- **Logs** : le système du projet (`log/slog` ou autre), jamais de `fmt.Println` de debug
  laissé en place.
- **Ressources** : `defer f.Close()` après vérification de l'erreur d'ouverture ; fermer
  les `resp.Body` HTTP, et mettre un timeout au client (`http.Client{Timeout: …}`).
- **Dépendances** : préférer la bibliothèque standard ; toute nouvelle dépendance est à
  signaler et à justifier. Pas de paquet marqué déprécié (alerte `SA1019`).

## Relire (reviewer)

À vérifier en plus des critères du brief :
- erreur ignorée ou écrasée, `%v` au lieu de `%w` là où l'appelant doit pouvoir tester ;
- goroutine sans arrêt, canal jamais fermé, accès concurrent sans verrou, `WaitGroup.Add`
  dans la goroutine ;
- `context` oublié ou stocké, appel bloquant sans timeout ;
- `defer` dans une boucle, `Body` non fermé, fichier non fermé ;
- test qui dort, dépend de l'ordre d'exécution, d'une horloge ou d'un état global ;
- `go.mod`/`go.sum` modifiés sans lien avec le changement, ou `go mod tidy` non fait ;
- API exportée ajoutée sans commentaire de documentation (`// Nom ...`) ;
- sorties de `golangci-lint` et `go vet` réellement lancées, pas supposées.

# Go

Les conventions du projet priment (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/`, `mise.toml`, `Makefile`,
`.golangci.yml`, code voisin). Ce qui suit comble ce qu'ils ne disent pas.

## Outillage

Repère d'abord les tâches du projet (`mise tasks`, `Makefile`, CI) : elles fixent les
versions et les options de lint. À défaut :

```bash
go build ./...
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./chemin/...        # si installé ; reprendre le .golangci.yml du projet
go test ./chemin/du/paquet/ -run 'TestNom' -count=1
go test -race ./chemin/...            # exige cgo et un compilateur C ; si absent, le dire
go mod tidy && git diff --stat go.mod go.sum   # après tout changement de dépendance
```

Version de Go : celle de `go.mod` (directive `go`/`toolchain`), pas celle que tu connais.
Une fonctionnalité récente du langage ou de la bibliothèque standard n'est utilisable que
si cette version la fournit.

## Tests

- Table-driven par défaut, un sous-test par cas nommé :
  ```go
  tests := []struct{ name string; in X; want Y; wantErr bool }{ … }
  for _, tt := range tests {
      t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) { … })
  }
  ```
- `t.Helper()` dans les fonctions utilitaires, `t.Cleanup` plutôt que `defer` dans les
  sous-tests, `t.TempDir()` et `t.Setenv()` pour isoler fichiers et environnement.
- `t.Parallel()` seulement si le test n'a aucun état partagé (variable globale, répertoire,
  port, `~/.config`).
- Compare avec la bibliothèque déjà utilisée par le projet (`testing` seul, `testify`,
  `go-cmp`) ; n'en ajoute pas une.
- Teste le comportement exposé (paquet `x_test` quand c'est possible), pas les détails
  internes. Pas de `time.Sleep` : injecte une horloge ou attends un signal.
- Une erreur attendue se vérifie avec `errors.Is` / `errors.As`, pas par comparaison de
  message.
- Fuzzing (`func FuzzX(f *testing.F)`) pour les parseurs et décodeurs d'entrées externes.
- Aucun test ne doit toucher au répertoire personnel, au trousseau, à Docker ni à un port
  fixe de l'hôte sans isolation.

## Écrire

- **Erreurs** : jamais ignorées (`_ =` justifié en commentaire). Enrobe avec contexte :
  `fmt.Errorf("lire %s: %w", path, err)`. Pas de `panic` hors initialisation.
  Pas de message commençant par une majuscule ni finissant par un point.
- **Interfaces** : petites, définies côté consommateur ; on accepte des interfaces, on
  retourne des types concrets.
- **`context.Context`** : premier paramètre, jamais stocké dans une structure, propagé aux
  appels bloquants ; `defer cancel()` juste après `WithCancel`/`WithTimeout`.
- **Goroutines** : chacune a un propriétaire et une condition d'arrêt (contexte, canal
  fermé, `errgroup`). Pas de goroutine lancée sans moyen de l'attendre. L'émetteur ferme
  le canal, jamais le récepteur.
- **Concurrence** : une map n'est pas sûre en écriture concurrente ; `sync.Mutex` plutôt
  qu'un canal pour protéger un état simple.
- **Boucles** : depuis Go 1.22, la variable de boucle est propre à chaque itération ; ne
  corrige pas ce qui n'est plus un défaut, mais respecte la version de `go.mod`.
- **`defer`** dans une boucle s'exécute à la sortie de la fonction : extraire le corps dans
  une fonction.
- **Slices et maps** : pré-allouer quand la taille est connue ; attention à l'aliasing
  après `append` ; une map `nil` se lit mais ne s'écrit pas.
- **Valeur zéro utile**, constructeurs `NewX` seulement si l'initialisation est
  non triviale. Options fonctionnelles seulement au-delà de 3 ou 4 paramètres optionnels.
- **Logs** : le système du projet (`log/slog` ou autre), jamais de `fmt.Println` de debug
  laissé en place.
- **Ressources** : `defer f.Close()` après vérification de l'erreur d'ouverture ; fermer
  les `resp.Body` HTTP, et mettre un timeout au client (`http.Client{Timeout: …}`).
- **Dépendances** : préférer la bibliothèque standard ; toute nouvelle dépendance est à
  signaler et à justifier. Pas de paquet marqué déprécié (alerte `SA1019`).

## Relire (reviewer)

À vérifier en plus des critères du brief :
- erreur ignorée ou écrasée, `%v` au lieu de `%w` là où l'appelant doit pouvoir tester ;
- goroutine sans arrêt, canal jamais fermé, accès concurrent sans verrou, `WaitGroup.Add`
  dans la goroutine ;
- `context` oublié ou stocké, appel bloquant sans timeout ;
- `defer` dans une boucle, `Body` non fermé, fichier non fermé ;
- test qui dort, dépend de l'ordre d'exécution, d'une horloge ou d'un état global ;
- `go.mod`/`go.sum` modifiés sans lien avec le changement, ou `go mod tidy` non fait ;
- API exportée ajoutée sans commentaire de documentation (`// Nom ...`) ;
- sorties de `golangci-lint` et `go vet` réellement lancées, pas supposées.

75	## Exigences non fonctionnelles
76	
77	- **Sécurité / confidentialité :** aucun test, sur aucune machine, ne lit ni n'écrit un secret réel
78	  de l'hôte. Le cas « garde-fou cassé » ne doit pas non plus atteindre le trousseau : le test du
79	  garde-fou installe d'abord un fournisseur go-keyring en erreur (`MockInitWithError`).
80	- **Déterminisme :** même résultat avec ou sans D-Bus, trousseau verrouillé ou non, sous
81	  `-count=2` et sous `-race` (AC 1, 2, 4).
82	- **Production inchangée :** même ordre de sélection, mêmes messages, mêmes erreurs ; la couture
83	  coûte une indirection par appel au trousseau. La panique du garde-fou est inaccessible hors d'un
84	  binaire de test (`testing.Testing()` est faux).
85	- **Exploitabilité :** l'échec nomme le test (panique dans le goroutine du test) ou à défaut le
86	  paquet (panique dans un autre goroutine : `FAIL <paquet>` + pile), et dit quoi faire.
87	- **Coût :** pas de nouvelle dépendance ; un import de `testing` dans le code de production de
88	  `internal/credentials` (H1, delta de taille du binaire à mesurer et à noter dans la PR).

91	
92	### Comment isoler
93	
94	| Option | Pour | Contre |
95	|---|---|---|
96	| **A. `keyring.MockInit()` dans chaque TestMain** | 2 lignes par paquet, aucun code de production | à refaire dans chaque paquet futur, rien ne le rappelle ; table go-keyring sans mutex, globale ; l'état survit entre tests et entre tours `-count=2` ; importe go-keyring hors de `credentials` ; ne garde rien |
97	| **B. Couture `HostStore` dans `credentials` + faux partagé `internal/testutil/fakekeyring`** (Install en TestMain, `Fresh(t)` par test) | un seul point de contact remplaçable ; faux DevDesk avec mutex, neuf par test ; permet le garde-fou d'exécution (l'adaptateur go-keyring sait qu'il est appelé) ; `Select` reste exercé de bout en bout, donc les tests de câblage gardent leur sens | une interface et une fonction exportées pour les tests ; un import `testing` en production |
98	| **C. Injection de la `Selection` (`var selectSecrets = credentials.Select` dans app et setup)** | aucune globale tierce ; couvre aussi git | deux coutures à neutraliser, même problème d'oubli que A ; ne protège pas un futur appelant de `Select` ; `TestCheckSecretBackendCmdReturnsAWellFormedMessage` deviendrait tautologique |
99	
100	**Recommandation : B.** C'est la seule option qui donne un garde-fou valable pour tout paquet,
101	présent et futur, sans liste à tenir : le garde est dans l'adaptateur, pas dans les tests. A est un
102	sous-cas de B sans garde-fou ; C déplace le problème au lieu de le fermer. Le faux vit dans
103	`internal/testutil/` (précédent : `loopback`, `connectproxy`), hors du binaire de production.
104	
105	### Comment détecter
106	
107	| Option | Pour | Contre |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| **Exécution** : l'adaptateur go-keyring (et `runCredential`) panique si `testing.Testing()` et que le paquet de test ne l'a pas autorisé | voit le transitif (`createContext` → `loadContext` → `Select`) ; ne dépend pas de l'hôte : échoue aussi sur une machine sans D-Bus ; nomme le test | ne voit que les chemins exécutés (mais un chemin non exécuté n'atteint pas le trousseau) |
110	| **Statique** (go/ast sur les `_test.go` / TestMain, comme `TestContainerGuard*`) | voit le code non exécuté | l'atteignabilité transitive de `Select` exige une analyse d'appels typée ; une liste de « paquets qui doivent appeler Install » serait à tenir à la main |
111	
112	**Recommandation : les deux, chacun pour ce qu'il voit.** Le garde d'exécution porte AC 3 (« via
113	`Select` / `KeyringAvailable` sans backend isolé ») ; un garde statique ferme les contournements
114	qu'il ne voit pas : import direct de go-keyring hors de `credentials` (« directement »), appel de
115	la couture depuis du code de production, import du faux depuis du code de production.

117	### Interaction avec HOME partagé et `-count=2`
118	
119	`fakekeyring.Install()` dans TestMain (filet pour tout test du paquet), et `fakekeyring.Fresh(t)`
120	appelé **par `isolateHome(t)`** dans les deux paquets : un test qui isole HOME isole aussi les
121	secrets, avec le même cycle de vie (`t.Cleanup`). Tous les tests qui construisent un routeur
122	passent déjà par `isolateHome` ; chaque test repart donc d'un magasin vide, à chaque tour de

1	# DEVDESK-610 — Les tests n'atteignent jamais le trousseau réel de l'hôte
2	
3	Story : isoler le backend de secrets dans `internal/ui/setup` et `internal/app`, et le garder par
4	un garde-fou. Hors périmètre : la durée de `internal/app` (~300 s).
5	
6	Ce plan n'est pas commité : les autres plans de `.claude/plans/` ne sont pas suivis par git.
7	
8	## Questions bloquantes
9	
10	Aucune. Trois choix sont tranchés ci-dessous par l'option la plus prudente (section « Hypothèses ») ;
11	l'orchestrateur peut les faire valider sans bloquer le démarrage.
12	
13	## État des lieux (lu dans le code)
14	
15	**Un seul point de contact avec le trousseau : `internal/credentials/keyring.go`.** `keyring.Get`,
16	`keyring.Set`, `keyring.Delete` (go-keyring v0.2.8) y sont appelés par `KeyringStorage.Save/Load/Delete`
17	et par `KeyringAvailable` (sonde `keyring.Get(devdesk, devdesk-availability-probe)`). Aucun autre
18	fichier du module n'importe `github.com/zalando/go-keyring`, sauf les tests de `internal/credentials`
19	(`keyring_test.go`, `select_test.go`).
20	
21	**go-keyring :** le fournisseur est une variable globale non exportée (`provider`) fixée par
22	`init()` selon l'OS (`secretServiceProvider` sous Linux). `MockInit()` / `MockInitWithError(err)` la
23	remplacent par une table en mémoire **sans mutex**, partagée par tout le processus. On ne peut pas
24	savoir de l'extérieur quel fournisseur est actif : un garde-fou d'exécution doit donc se placer
25	dans notre propre code, avant l'appel à go-keyring.
26	
27	**Chemins de production vers le trousseau** (`entire graph impact --symbol Select`) :
28	
29	| Appelant | Fichier | Atteint par les tests de |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| `New` | `internal/app/app.go:245` | aucun (lit `term.GetSize`, les tests passent par `newWithSize`) |
32	| `App.resolveSecretBackend` ← `handleConfigSaved` | `internal/app/configuration.go:88` | `internal/app` |
33	| `loadContext` ← `switchContext`, `createContext` | `internal/app/context.go:115` (+ `MigrateLegacySecrets` ligne 116, qui **écrit** dans le store choisi) | `internal/app` (dont `TestCtxNewWithANameClosesTheLineWithoutRefusal`) |
34	| `validateTokenCmd` ← `finishWizard` | `internal/ui/setup/commands.go:43` | `internal/ui/setup` (si un test exécute la Cmd) |
35	| `checkSecretBackendCmd` ← `recheckSecretBackendCmd` | `internal/ui/setup/commands.go:67` | `internal/ui/setup` (`TestCheckSecretBackendCmdReturnsAWellFormedMessage`) |
36	
37	`KeyringAvailable` et `NewKeyringStorage` n'ont pas d'autre appelant que `Select`.
38	
39	**Audit des autres importateurs de `internal/credentials`** (grep des imports et des appels) :
40	
41	| Paquet | Usage | Atteint le trousseau ? |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| `internal/mcp` | `ResolveToken(sel Selection)` ; tests : `Selection{Storage: NewMemoryStorage()}`, `SessionOnly` | non : la Selection est injectée |
44	| `internal/ui/forge/auth` | `New(cfg, secrets Selection, …)` ; tests : `persisted(storage)`, `SessionOnly` | non |
45	| `internal/template`, `internal/forge/session`, `internal/ui/workspaces`, `internal/ui/security`, `internal/ui/forge/explorer`, `internal/ui/templates`, `internal/shared` | reçoivent un `Storage` / une `Selection` ; tests : `NewMemoryStorage` | non |
46	| `internal/engine`, `internal/ui/configuration`, `internal/config` | commentaires seulement | non |
47	| `main` (`main_test.go`) | `TestForcedColorProfile`, `TestEnsureDefaultContext…` : n'appellent pas `app.New` | non (à confirmer par l'étape 1) |
48	
49	Seuls `internal/app` et `internal/ui/setup` atteignent donc le trousseau réel aujourd'hui. Le
50	garde-fou d'exécution de l'étape 1 le **prouve** au lieu de le supposer : lancé sur `./...`, il
51	nomme tout test qui l'atteint.
52	
53	**Deuxième porte vers le Secret Service : `git credential`.** `Select("auto")` retombe sur
54	`gitHelperUsable` quand la sonde échoue, et `GitCredentialStorage.Save/Load/Delete` lance
55	`git credential approve|fill|reject` (`runCredential`, `git_credential.go:114`), qui appelle l'assistant
56	configuré ; un assistant `libsecret` parle à D-Bus. HOME est déjà un répertoire temporaire dans
57	`internal/app` et `internal/ui/setup` (TestMain), donc `~/.gitconfig` n'est pas lu, mais
58	`/etc/gitconfig` et le `.git/config` du dépôt le sont. Avec un trousseau factice joignable, `auto`
59	n'atteint jamais git ; seul un test qui épingle `git-credential` puis sauvegarde le ferait. Le
60	garde-fou couvre aussi `runCredential` (hypothèse H2).
61	
62	**Pièges existants qui interagissent :**
63	
64	- HOME partagé (DEVDESK-36/38) : `TestMain` fixe HOME une fois par processus ; `isolateHome(t)`
65	  (`internal/app/harness_test.go:172`, `internal/ui/setup/model_test.go:48`) le refait par test.
66	  `routerAt` et `argRouter` l'appellent. Le magasin de secrets est le second état persistant de
67	  l'hôte : il doit suivre la même règle, sinon `-count=2` retrouve le jeton écrit au premier tour.
68	- Aucun `t.Parallel()` dans `internal/app` ni `internal/ui/setup` : un remplacement global par test
69	  est sûr (même contrainte que `t.Setenv`).
70	- Aucun `recover()` dans le code de production : une panique dans une Cmd exécutée par
71	  `testutil.Msgs` (synchrone) remonte au `tRunner` du test, qui imprime `--- FAIL: TestNom`.
72	- Précédent des coutures neutralisées en TestMain : `containerForward` dans `internal/app`
73	  (DEVDESK-583).
74	
75	## Exigences non fonctionnelles
76	
77	- **Sécurité / confidentialité :** aucun test, sur aucune machine, ne lit ni n'écrit un secret réel
78	  de l'hôte. Le cas « garde-fou cassé » ne doit pas non plus atteindre le trousseau : le test du
79	  garde-fou installe d'abord un fournisseur go-keyring en erreur (`MockInitWithError`).
80	- **Déterminisme :** même résultat avec ou sans D-Bus, trousseau verrouillé ou non, sous
81	  `-count=2` et sous `-race` (AC 1, 2, 4).
82	- **Production inchangée :** même ordre de sélection, mêmes messages, mêmes erreurs ; la couture
83	  coûte une indirection par appel au trousseau. La panique du garde-fou est inaccessible hors d'un
84	  binaire de test (`testing.Testing()` est faux).
85	- **Exploitabilité :** l'échec nomme le test (panique dans le goroutine du test) ou à défaut le
86	  paquet (panique dans un autre goroutine : `FAIL <paquet>` + pile), et dit quoi faire.
87	- **Coût :** pas de nouvelle dépendance ; un import de `testing` dans le code de production de
88	  `internal/credentials` (H1, delta de taille du binaire à mesurer et à noter dans la PR).
89	
90	## Options comparées
91	
92	### Comment isoler
93	
94	| Option | Pour | Contre |
95	|---|---|---|
96	| **A. `keyring.MockInit()` dans chaque TestMain** | 2 lignes par paquet, aucun code de production | à refaire dans chaque paquet futur, rien ne le rappelle ; table go-keyring sans mutex, globale ; l'état survit entre tests et entre tours `-count=2` ; importe go-keyring hors de `credentials` ; ne garde rien |
97	| **B. Couture `HostStore` dans `credentials` + faux partagé `internal/testutil/fakekeyring`** (Install en TestMain, `Fresh(t)` par test) | un seul point de contact remplaçable ; faux DevDesk avec mutex, neuf par test ; permet le garde-fou d'exécution (l'adaptateur go-keyring sait qu'il est appelé) ; `Select` reste exercé de bout en bout, donc les tests de câblage gardent leur sens | une interface et une fonction exportées pour les tests ; un import `testing` en production |
98	| **C. Injection de la `Selection` (`var selectSecrets = credentials.Select` dans app et setup)** | aucune globale tierce ; couvre aussi git | deux coutures à neutraliser, même problème d'oubli que A ; ne protège pas un futur appelant de `Select` ; `TestCheckSecretBackendCmdReturnsAWellFormedMessage` deviendrait tautologique |
99	
100	**Recommandation : B.** C'est la seule option qui donne un garde-fou valable pour tout paquet,
101	présent et futur, sans liste à tenir : le garde est dans l'adaptateur, pas dans les tests. A est un
102	sous-cas de B sans garde-fou ; C déplace le problème au lieu de le fermer. Le faux vit dans
103	`internal/testutil/` (précédent : `loopback`, `connectproxy`), hors du binaire de production.
104	
105	### Comment détecter
106	
107	| Option | Pour | Contre |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| **Exécution** : l'adaptateur go-keyring (et `runCredential`) panique si `testing.Testing()` et que le paquet de test ne l'a pas autorisé | voit le transitif (`createContext` → `loadContext` → `Select`) ; ne dépend pas de l'hôte : échoue aussi sur une machine sans D-Bus ; nomme le test | ne voit que les chemins exécutés (mais un chemin non exécuté n'atteint pas le trousseau) |
110	| **Statique** (go/ast sur les `_test.go` / TestMain, comme `TestContainerGuard*`) | voit le code non exécuté | l'atteignabilité transitive de `Select` exige une analyse d'appels typée ; une liste de « paquets qui doivent appeler Install » serait à tenir à la main |
111	
112	**Recommandation : les deux, chacun pour ce qu'il voit.** Le garde d'exécution porte AC 3 (« via
113	`Select` / `KeyringAvailable` sans backend isolé ») ; un garde statique ferme les contournements
114	qu'il ne voit pas : import direct de go-keyring hors de `credentials` (« directement »), appel de
115	la couture depuis du code de production, import du faux depuis du code de production.
116	
117	### Interaction avec HOME partagé et `-count=2`
118	
119	`fakekeyring.Install()` dans TestMain (filet pour tout test du paquet), et `fakekeyring.Fresh(t)`
120	appelé **par `isolateHome(t)`** dans les deux paquets : un test qui isole HOME isole aussi les
121	secrets, avec le même cycle de vie (`t.Cleanup`). Tous les tests qui construisent un routeur
122	passent déjà par `isolateHome` ; chaque test repart donc d'un magasin vide, à chaque tour de
123	`-count=N`.
124	
125	## Modèle
126	
127	```go
128	// internal/credentials/hoststore.go (nouveau)
129	
130	// HostStore is the host secret manager as KeyringStorage and KeyringAvailable
131	// see it. A missing entry is an error for which errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound).
132	type HostStore interface {
133	    Get(service, account string) (string, error)
134	    Set(service, account, secret string) error
135	    Delete(service, account string) error
136	}
137	
138	// currentHost returns the store in use: goKeyring{} unless a test swapped it.
139	func currentHost() HostStore
140	
141	// SwapHostStoreForTest installs s and returns the store it replaces. It panics
142	// outside a test binary. Only _test.go files and internal/testutil/fakekeyring
143	// may call it (TestHostStoreGuardSwapOnlyFromTests).
144	func SwapHostStoreForTest(s HostStore) HostStore
145	
146	// goKeyring is the production HostStore: zalando/go-keyring, mapping
147	// keyring.ErrNotFound to ErrNotFound. Every method calls refuseUnderTest first.
148	type goKeyring struct{}
149	
150	// hostReachableUnderTest is set only by internal/credentials' own TestMain,
151	// whose tests mock go-keyring themselves and run git against a hermetic config.
152	var hostReachableUnderTest atomic.Bool
153	
154	// refuseUnderTest panics with hostStoreUnderTestMessage when the code runs in
155	// a test binary that has not allowed the real host store.
156	func refuseUnderTest(op string)
157	
158	const hostStoreUnderTestMessage = "credentials: a test reached the host secret store (%s) " +
159	    "without isolation; call fakekeyring.Install() in TestMain or fakekeyring.Fresh(t) " +
160	    "(DEVDESK-610, docs/architecture/configuration.md)"
161	```
162	
163	Le stockage courant est protégé (mutex ou `atomic.Pointer` sur une boîte) : `-race` ne doit rien
164	signaler si une Cmd lit `currentHost()` pendant qu'un `t.Cleanup` restaure le précédent.

168	
169	type Store struct{ /* mu sync.Mutex; entries map[service+"\x00"+account]string; err error */ }
170	
171	func NewStore() *Store                      // joignable, vide
172	func NewUnreachableStore(err error) *Store  // chaque opération renvoie err
173	func (s *Store) Get(service, account string) (string, error) // manquant : wraps credentials.ErrNotFound
174	func (s *Store) Set(service, account, secret string) error
175	func (s *Store) Delete(service, account string) error         // manquant : wraps credentials.ErrNotFound
176	func (s *Store) Entries() map[string]string                  // copie, pour les assertions
177

184	`keyring` épinglée. En `auto`, `Select` essaierait ensuite git, dont la réponse dépend de

20	// HostStore seam (hoststore.go). The runtime guard (refuseUnderTest) only sees
21	// the code paths a test executes; this one reads every .go file of the module
22	// (go/parser, no type information) and reports three ways the isolation can be
23	// bypassed or leak into production:
24	//
25	//	K1  an import of github.com/zalando/go-keyring outside internal/credentials/hoststore.go
26	//	    and the _test.go files of internal/credentials. A test elsewhere that talks to
27	//	    go-keyring (mock or not) bypasses the seam and the fake.
28	//	K2  a reference to credentials.SwapHostStoreForTest in a non-test file, except
29	//	    internal/testutil/fakekeyring and internal/credentials itself. The seam is for
30	//	    tests; production code must never replace the host store.
31	//	K3  an import of internal/testutil/fakekeyring from a non-test file (it imports
32	//	    "testing" and must not reach a production binary). No exception.
33	//
34	// What the guard cannot see (a shadowed package name, an import path built at
35	// run time, a test that shells out to a binary that reaches the keyring) is
36	// listed in docs/architecture/configuration.md.

84	// the last element of its path. "_" and "." are returned as is.

92	// scanHostStoreSource parses src as the file name (a slash path from the module
93	// root) and returns its violations ordered by line, then rule.
94	func scanHostStoreSource(name string, src []byte) ([]hostViolation, error) {
95		fset := token.NewFileSet()
96		f, err := parser.ParseFile(fset, name, src, parser.SkipObjectResolution)
97		if err != nil {
98			return nil, err
99		}
100		isTest := strings.HasSuffix(name, "_test.go")
101		dir := path.Dir(name)
102	
103		var out []hostViolation
104		add := func(pos token.Pos, rule string) {
105			out = append(out, hostViolation{File: name, Line: fset.Position(pos).Line, Rule: rule})
106		}
107	
108		credName := ""   // local name of internal/credentials ("" = not imported)
109		credDot := false // internal/credentials is dot-imported
110		for _, spec := range f.Imports {
111			p, err := strconv.Unquote(spec.Path.Value)
112			if err != nil {
113				continue
114			}
115			switch p {
116			case goKeyringPath:
117				if name != hostStoreFile && (!isTest || dir != credentialsDir) {
118					add(spec.Pos(), ruleKeyringImport)
119				}
120			case fakeKeyringPath:
121				if !isTest {
122					add(spec.Pos(), ruleFakeInProd)
123				}
124			case credentialsPath:
125				credName = importLocalName(spec, p)
126				credDot = credName == "."
127			}
128		}
129	
130		swapAllowed := isTest || dir == fakeKeyringDir || dir == credentialsDir
131		if credName != "" && !swapAllowed {
132			ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
133				switch n := n.(type) {
134				case *ast.SelectorExpr:
135					if id, ok := n.X.(*ast.Ident); ok && !credDot && id.Name == credName && n.Sel.Name == swapSeamName {
136						add(n.Sel.Pos(), ruleSwapInProd)
137					}
138				case *ast.Ident:
139					if credDot && n.Name == swapSeamName {
140						add(n.Pos(), ruleSwapInProd)
141					}
142				}

144			})
145		}

147		slices.SortStableFunc(out, func(a, b hostViolation) int {
148			if a.Line != b.Line {
149				return a.Line - b.Line
150			}
151			return strings.Compare(a.Rule, b.Rule)
152		})
153		return out, nil
154	}

158	// root. It also returns the number of files read.
159	func scanHostStoreTree(root string) ([]hostViolation, int, error) {
160		var all []hostViolation
161		files := 0
162		err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
163			if err != nil {
164				return err
165			}
166			rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, p)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)

```bash

mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build

mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package

mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

mise run vet          # Run go vet

mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies

CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511).** The tests of the Nexus
code (`internal/imagesearch`, `internal/registrymgr`) replay answers measured on
the bench from `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/`, through
`internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, no cluster and
no secret. Every fixture is leak-checked in the suite; set
`DEVDESK_FIXTURE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one term per
line) to add names the repository must not carry. A fixture whose Nexus version
differs from `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` fails the suite: regenerate
with `mise run nexus-bench:record`. See `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)

- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511).** The tests of the Nexus
code (`internal/imagesearch`, `internal/registrymgr`) replay answers measured on
the bench from `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/`, through
`internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, no cluster and
no secret. Every fixture is leak-checked in the suite; set
`DEVDESK_FIXTURE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one term per
line) to add names the repository must not carry. A fixture whose Nexus version
differs from `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` fails the suite: regenerate
with `mise run nexus-bench:record`. See `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

</system-reminder>

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

1	package credentials
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"go/ast"
6		"go/parser"
7		"go/token"
8		"io/fs"
9		"os"
10		"path"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"slices"
13		"strconv"
14		"strings"
15		"sync"
16		"testing"
17	)
18	
19	// DEVDESK-610: the static guard that keeps the host secret store behind the
20	// HostStore seam (hoststore.go). The runtime guard (refuseUnderTest) only sees
21	// the code paths a test executes; this one reads every .go file of the module
22	// (go/parser, no type information) and reports three ways the isolation can be
23	// bypassed or leak into production:
24	//
25	//	K1  an import of github.com/zalando/go-keyring outside internal/credentials/hoststore.go
26	//	    and the _test.go files of internal/credentials. A test elsewhere that talks to
27	//	    go-keyring (mock or not) bypasses the seam and the fake.
28	//	K2  a reference to credentials.SwapHostStoreForTest in a non-test file, except
29	//	    internal/testutil/fakekeyring and internal/credentials itself. The seam is for
30	//	    tests; production code must never replace the host store.
31	//	K3  an import of internal/testutil/fakekeyring from a non-test file (it imports
32	//	    "testing" and must not reach a production binary). No exception.
33	//
34	// What the guard cannot see (a shadowed package name, an import path built at
35	// run time, a test that shells out to a binary that reaches the keyring) is
36	// listed in docs/architecture/configuration.md.
37	
38	const (
39		ruleKeyringImport = "K1"
40		ruleSwapInProd    = "K2"
41		ruleFakeInProd    = "K3"
42	
43		goKeyringPath    = "github.com/zalando/go-keyring"
44		credentialsPath  = "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/credentials"
45		fakeKeyringPath  = "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/testutil/fakekeyring"
46		swapSeamName     = "SwapHostStoreForTest"
47		credentialsDir   = "internal/credentials"
48		hostStoreFile    = "internal/credentials/hoststore.go"
49		fakeKeyringDir   = "internal/testutil/fakekeyring"
50		hostGuardMinimum = 50
51	)
52	
53	var hostStoreRules = []string{ruleKeyringImport, ruleSwapInProd, ruleFakeInProd}
54	
55	// hostStoreExcludedDirs are skipped at any depth below the module root, like the
56	// other source guards.
57	var hostStoreExcludedDirs = []string{".worktrees", ".git", "vendor", "testdata", "docs-site", "node_modules"}
58	
59	// hostViolation is one place where the host secret store is reached or the seam
60	// is used outside what the rules allow.
61	type hostViolation struct {
62		File string // slash path from the module root
63		Line int
64		Rule string // "K1".."K3"
65	}
66	
67	// String is the report line: file:line: rule, then what to do.
68	func (v hostViolation) String() string {
69		return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d: %s %s", v.File, v.Line, v.Rule, hostStoreAdvice[v.Rule])
70	}
71	
72	// hostStoreAdvice names the rule broken and the way out, so a failure needs no
73	// trip to the documentation.
74	var hostStoreAdvice = map[string]string{
75		ruleKeyringImport: "imports github.com/zalando/go-keyring outside internal/credentials; " +
76			"isolate with fakekeyring.Install() or fakekeyring.Fresh(t) and go through credentials (DEVDESK-610)",
77		ruleSwapInProd: "calls credentials.SwapHostStoreForTest from a non-test file; " +
78			"the seam is for _test.go files and internal/testutil/fakekeyring only (DEVDESK-610)",
79		ruleFakeInProd: "imports internal/testutil/fakekeyring from a non-test file; " +
80			"it imports \"testing\" and belongs to _test.go files only (DEVDESK-610)",
81	}
82	
83	// importLocalName is the identifier an import binds in the file: its alias, or
84	// the last element of its path. "_" and "." are returned as is.
85	func importLocalName(spec *ast.ImportSpec, importPath string) string {
86		if spec.Name != nil {
87			return spec.Name.Name
88		}
89		return path.Base(importPath)
90	}
91	
92	// scanHostStoreSource parses src as the file name (a slash path from the module
93	// root) and returns its violations ordered by line, then rule.
94	func scanHostStoreSource(name string, src []byte) ([]hostViolation, error) {
95		fset := token.NewFileSet()
96		f, err := parser.ParseFile(fset, name, src, parser.SkipObjectResolution)
97		if err != nil {
98			return nil, err
99		}
100		isTest := strings.HasSuffix(name, "_test.go")
101		dir := path.Dir(name)
102	
103		var out []hostViolation
104		add := func(pos token.Pos, rule string) {
105			out = append(out, hostViolation{File: name, Line: fset.Position(pos).Line, Rule: rule})
106		}
107	
108		credName := ""   // local name of internal/credentials ("" = not imported)
109		credDot := false // internal/credentials is dot-imported
110		for _, spec := range f.Imports {
111			p, err := strconv.Unquote(spec.Path.Value)
112			if err != nil {
113				continue
114			}
115			switch p {
116			case goKeyringPath:
117				if name != hostStoreFile && (!isTest || dir != credentialsDir) {
118					add(spec.Pos(), ruleKeyringImport)
119				}
120			case fakeKeyringPath:
121				if !isTest {
122					add(spec.Pos(), ruleFakeInProd)
123				}
124			case credentialsPath:
125				credName = importLocalName(spec, p)
126				credDot = credName == "."
127			}
128		}
129	
130		swapAllowed := isTest || dir == fakeKeyringDir || dir == credentialsDir
131		if credName != "" && !swapAllowed {
132			ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
133				switch n := n.(type) {
134				case *ast.SelectorExpr:
135					if id, ok := n.X.(*ast.Ident); ok && !credDot && id.Name == credName && n.Sel.Name == swapSeamName {
136						add(n.Sel.Pos(), ruleSwapInProd)
137					}
138				case *ast.Ident:
139					if credDot && n.Name == swapSeamName {
140						add(n.Pos(), ruleSwapInProd)
141					}
142				}
143				return true
144			})
145		}
146	
147		slices.SortStableFunc(out, func(a, b hostViolation) int {
148			if a.Line != b.Line {
149				return a.Line - b.Line
150			}
151			return strings.Compare(a.Rule, b.Rule)
152		})
153		return out, nil
154	}
155	
156	// scanHostStoreTree scans every .go file under root (test files included: K1
157	// applies to them), skipping hostStoreExcludedDirs matched on the names below
158	// root. It also returns the number of files read.
159	func scanHostStoreTree(root string) ([]hostViolation, int, error) {
160		var all []hostViolation
161		files := 0
162		err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
163			if err != nil {
164				return err
165			}
166			rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, p)
167			if err != nil {
168				return err
169			}
170			rel = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
171			if d.IsDir() {
172				if rel != "." && slices.Contains(hostStoreExcludedDirs, d.Name()) {
173					return filepath.SkipDir
174				}
175				return nil
176			}
177			if !strings.HasSuffix(rel, ".go") {
178				return nil
179			}
180			src, err := os.ReadFile(p)
181			if err != nil {
182				return err
183			}
184			vs, err := scanHostStoreSource(rel, src)
185			if err != nil {
186				return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", rel, err)
187			}
188			files++
189			all = append(all, vs...)
190			return nil

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**

- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`
